title: Finite structures: parity, connectedness and first-order limits
summary: Prove that no first-order sentence detects parity on finite orders or connectedness on finite graphs, using an explicit game strategy and formula translation.
abstract: A finite order has a definite number of points, but one first-order sentence cannot tell whether that number is even for every possible size. We prove this by matching points in long orders while keeping their remaining gaps large enough for the rounds still to come. The same obstruction reaches graphs: joining every point to the point two steps ahead in a cyclic reading of an order produces a connected graph exactly when the order has odd size. Translating edge statements into order formulas then shows that connectedness, and even reachability between two specified vertices, has no uniform first-order definition on finite graphs. A fixed size bound changes the answer, because then only finitely many possible path lengths need to be considered.
